# Length-3704 W(2,7) attempt (2026-07-27)

## Status

No valid length-3704 witness was found. The best independently recounted state
has exactly one monochromatic seven-term arithmetic progression:

- one-based start: `2`
- common difference: `617`
- color: `0`
- points: `2, 619, 1236, 1853, 2470, 3087, 3704`
- coloring SHA-256: `af812d405f4cd4a5e4da8ee62f77d76409de22c328c29fe6d052b279912d5882`
- minimum symmetry distance from the verified 3703 record plus a zero: `6`

This is a failing search state, not a record submission.

## Work completed

- Exhaustively checked 130,722,880 candidates across single insertion
  symmetries, a constrained delete-one/insert-two neighborhood, structured
  transforms, block/boundary shears, and the complete affine block
  deformation family. The minimum remained one conflict.
- Closed several restricted algebraic families with exact SAT receipts:
  the six-block `p=617` macro family, the `p=619/q=103` and
  `p=631/q=105` cyclotomic families, and the affine orientation family.
  These are restricted-family UNSAT results, not a proof about length 3704.
- Ran a refreezing column implicit-hitting-set search for 180 seconds. It
  produced 15,595 distinct UNSAT cores, but the raw cores remained about
  190-210 columns wide and the master boundary stayed at only 4-5 free
  columns.
- Ran monotone column-core release for 180 seconds. It reached 444 free
  columns and then repeatedly returned UNKNOWN.
- Rebuilt and self-tested the point-level E2 core-release solver, then ran
  `batch=1` for 180 seconds. It still expanded to 3,486 free points before
  repeatedly returning UNKNOWN, showing that smaller batches do not fix the
  monotone-release degeneration.
- Added a true `--start-state` path to the full local-search program and
  verified it in release and ASan/UBSan builds. Twelve 300-second runs
  completed 200,140,656 flips. Ordinary runs moved the E1 frontier from
  symmetry distance 2 to 6. Deep runs raised the energy ceiling from 48 to
  128-320 and crossed the previously observed E≈99 barrier, but returned only
  to E1 states at distance at most 6.

## Failure mode

The nearest states are not one-flip repairs. Breaking the remaining
difference-617 progression creates several new monochromatic progressions, so
the search needs a coordinated move. Monotone core release discards too much
structure, while the current IHS master receives cores too wide to guide a
useful boundary.

A promising continuation would retain and subsume full cores, progressively
shrink selected cores, use an exact hitting-set check only when the greedy
master stalls, and checkpoint the complete master/free-set state. Re-running
the existing seeds or merely increasing the monotone release budget is not
expected to help.
